existing_full_tradition.name: Free Tekno
existing_full_tradition.lineage: European free-party sound-system music formed 1992-1995 when UK travellers' rigs (Spiral Tribe, Bedlam, Circus Warp) relocated to France, Italy and the Czech Republic after the Criminal Justice Act, codified at teknivals as 150-180 BPM hardware-sequenced 4/4 with a distorted overdriven kick, dry stabbing acid and metallic percussion loops, no vocal, and hour-long DJ-less live sets played on self-built rigs.

existing_full_extras.description: Free tekno emerged from the mid-1990s European free-party circuit, made by and for travelling sound systems playing unlicensed teknivals in warehouses, quarries and fields. Its sonic signature is a heavily saturated, near-square kick drum at 150-180 BPM, relentlessly looped acid and noise-percussion layers with almost no harmonic movement, and a deliberately raw mix optimised for enormous outdoor stacks rather than club monitors. It is faster and dirtier than Detroit or Berlin techno, and unlike gabber it stays rhythmically austere rather than anthemic, with tracks pressed to white-label vinyl or traded on unmarked CDs outside any commercial industry.
